VibePascal v56 Linux x86_64 compiler -- an inferred inline var initialised from
a real constant is a Double, whatever the constant's value happens to be
Source commit: a187bbac34 (merge of inlinevar-real-default)
Compiler fix:  f06e46d8eb  (compiler/pstatmnt.pas, compiler/defutil.pas, compiler/ncnv.pas)
Parent release: v55 (eae5d3e919a26a7db19937da10da1c8b610b17da)
Built: 2026-09-10, native self-host fixpoint on x86_64-linux
ppcx64 md5:    E6DE1F00ECCB9B5CCF028BEE7E7342AD

Contents: bin/ppcx64 only -- a COMPILER-BINARY refresh meant to drop into an
existing VibePascal source/unit tree on Linux.  No RTL change, no package
change, no PPU format change, so an existing v52/v53/v54/v55 Linux unit set
stays valid and the utility binaries (ppudump/ppumove/fpcres/...) are unchanged
and not re-shipped.

WHAT WAS BROKEN
  An inline var with no type annotation took its type from the real constant
  you initialised it with, and that type changes with the VALUE:

      var a := 1.0;      // Single   -  4 bytes,  7 digits
      var b := 0.1;      // Extended - 10 bytes, 19 digits
      var c := 1.0/3.0;  // Single, or Extended under {$mode delphi}
      var d := 1/2;      // Double

  Four declarations side by side, four different types, none of them the one
  Delphi or an explicit `var x: Double := ...` gives.  The 4-byte case is the
  one that bites: `var pi := 3.14159265358979` quietly kept about seven digits,
  and the same variable widened to fifteen as soon as somebody edited the
  literal to one a Single cannot represent exactly.  Lars hit the other end of
  it in the Lazarus IDE, where code completion and the compiler disagreed.

CHANGE
  An un-annotated inline var initialised from a real CONSTANT now infers the
  default real type, Double.  It is the third rule of the family v54 started:
  `var i := -1` -> NativeInt, `var s := 'x'` -> the default string type, and now
  a real constant -> the default real type.  Inference gives you the DEFAULT
  type of a kind, not the narrowest one that happens to fit today's literal.
  Double and not Extended because Extended is an x87-only 80-bit type and
  Delphi makes Extended an alias of Double on every 64-bit target we ship.

  Deliberately unchanged:
   - RANGE is never lost.  1.0e400 and 1.0e-4000 keep the wider type they were
     given; a Double would silently hold +Inf and 0.  Precision digits can be
     lost, because that is what asking for a Double means.
   - A variable or non-constant expression keeps its own type, as Delphi infers
     it: `var m := someSingle` is still a Single.
   - An explicit `single(1.0)` still wins.  Making that true was part of the
     fix: a cast to the type a constant already had used to be dropped without
     recording that the user asked for it.
   - Currency and Comp are untouched, and `var d := 1/2` was already a Double.
   - How real CONSTANTS themselves are typed is NOT touched.  That is stock FPC
     behaviour ($MINFPCONSTPREC default s32real, $EXCESSPRECISION on in delphi
     mode), byte-identical to upstream, and still reachable explicitly.

VERIFIED ON THIS PLATFORM (x86_64-linux, native -- not emulated, not wine)
  Isolated throwaway A/B compilers, real toolchain untouched.  The baseline
  built that way came out byte-identical to the published v55 Linux binary
  (19F526BD6BE0EC63FCA96C4D1B77E19D), which is what makes the A/B trustworthy.
   - tinlinevarrealinfer1.pp: 57 checks over 10 structural contexts (free
     procedure, method, nested block, nested procedure, with-block, for-loop
     body, except and finally, while/repeat/case, closure capture, main program
     body) crossed with the MODE axis, because delphi mode widens a constant
     fold differently:
        -Munleashed       baseline 37 failures -> 0 of 57
        -Mdelphi          baseline 36 failures -> 0 of 54
        -Mdelphiunicode   baseline 36 failures -> 0 of 54
     VALUES are asserted as well as sizes, including through a closure capture:
     an inferred variable must hold exactly what the declared one holds.
   - tinlinevarrealinfer2.pp (%FAIL): `for var i := 1.0 to 2.0` is still
     rejected, cleanly, with no internal error.
   - full tests/test corpus, 1982 tests: 1981 SAME, 0 DIFF, after a
     baseline-against-baseline control run that was also 0 DIFF.
   - self-host fixpoint: stage2 == stage3, byte-identical (this md5).
   - the neighbouring inference rules are unmoved: tinlinevarnativeint1 45/45
     and tinlinevarstrinfer1 20/20, both under -Munleashed and -Mdelphiunicode.
  Re-run from the EXTRACTED tarball rather than the build tree, so what is
  measured is what is shipped.

STILL ON v55 OR OLDER AFTER THIS RELEASE
  aarch64-linux, arm-linux, x86_64-darwin and aarch64-darwin carry v55, and
  arm-linux-cross and i386-linux-cross carry v54.  None of them has this real
  inference change yet; each needs a cross rebuild from a187bbac34.  That is
  tracked.  Those packages are honestly labelled, but do not read this release
  as "the fix is everywhere".
